articles.title: Home Assistant keeps energy totals within the chosen dates
articles.dek: Viewing a home from another timezone no longer adds a neighbouring day to the energy calculation.
body: Home Assistant stops counting an extra day in multi-day energy totals when the browser and home server use different timezones. A browser ahead of the server could include the day before the selected range; one behind could include the day after it.

Petar Petrov aligns daily and monthly energy requests with the home server’s calendar. A companion correction keeps the chosen dates and times in place in Energy, History and Logbook when the profile uses the server timezone.

pullRequests.title: Fix energy ranges counting an extra day across time zones

articles.title: Home Assistant withdraws the planned Assist account choice
articles.dek: The setting reported yesterday is removed from development work because its design was not approved.
body: Home Assistant withdraws the Assist account choice reported in the September 28 edition. The work under development allowed a voice assistant to act as a selected household member, so integrations could choose that person’s linked account.

Paulus Schoutsen removes both the setting and its underlying support, stating that the approach was not approved in the architecture discussion. This reverses the planned assistant-level choice; it does not withdraw Music Assistant’s own personal favourites and account controls.

articles.title: Offline Modbus equipment stops delaying Home Assistant startup
articles.dek: An unreachable device could hold up the final startup phase for more than five minutes.
body: Home Assistant stops waiting for an offline Modbus device before finishing startup. An unplugged or unreachable meter, inverter or other device could keep the final startup phase waiting until its timeout; four reports measured about 318 seconds.

Franck Nijhof moves connection attempts and regular polling into the background without changing their timing. Removing or disabling an entity also cancels its pending wait, so an absent device does not leave work running for a deleted entity.

pullRequests.title: Fix Modbus entities holding up Home Assistant startup while their device is unreachable

articles.title: Apple Watch Assist follows the iPhone’s local speech choices
articles.dek: Watch requests can use iPhone transcription and spoken replies generated on the watch.
body: Home Assistant’s Apple Watch assistant follows the local speech and mute choices set for Assist on the iPhone. With local speech recognition enabled, the paired iPhone transcribes the watch recording instead of sending it for server transcription.

When local speech output is selected, the watch speaks the answer itself. Muting replies or choosing local speech also stops the request for a server-generated voice response. Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves supplies the change.

articles.title: Assist expands Basque control across music, timers and household tasks
articles.dek: New commands reach shopping lists, heating, robot cleaners and delayed actions.
body: Basque speakers gain a much wider set of Assist commands, from starting and adjusting timers to controlling music, heating and robot cleaners. Shopping-list commands add items or mark them complete, while delayed commands can ask for the lights to turn off after a chosen interval.

Urtzi Odriozola also adds questions about the weather, date, time and whether someone is home. This extends the lighting controls reported on September 25 with everyday tasks across the house; it does not introduce Basque voice control for the first time.

articles.title: Home Assistant controls compatible OSRAM lights with infrared
articles.dek: An existing infrared emitter can send power, preset colour and effect commands.
body: Home Assistant adds infrared control for compatible OSRAM and LEDVANCE colour lights using the supported 24-button remote command set. An infrared emitter already configured in Home Assistant supplies on-and-off control, preset colours and Flash, Strobe or Smooth effects.

An optional receiver can follow supported commands from the physical remote and update the displayed state. Infrared cannot confirm that the light received a command, and brightness control is not supported. Colours chosen on the colour wheel map to the nearest remote preset.
Dominik supplies the integration and makes a first contribution to Home Assistant’s website with its accompanying guide.

articles.title: Music Assistant carries a podcast queue onto home speakers
articles.dek: Pocket Casts folders play their episodes and preserve saved positions as the queue advances.
body: Music Assistant can play podcast episodes from a browse folder, including Pocket Casts’ Up Next and In Progress lists. Those folders previously discarded episodes and could report that there was nothing to play, blocking an automation that continued a mobile listening queue on a home speaker.

Episodes begin at the listener’s saved position. A companion correction also applies saved positions when the queue advances automatically to another podcast episode or audiobook, instead of starting it at zero and risking a later pause overwriting its bookmark.
Folder playback still follows the queue’s shuffle setting. Ordinary radio stations in a folder are supported too, but dynamic stations that generate their own tracks remain outside this route.

articles.title: Music Assistant shows the albums missing from your collection
articles.dek: An artist’s MusicBrainz discography can lead to an album on a connected music service.
body: Music Assistant’s artist page gains a Discography row showing albums, EPs and singles catalogued by MusicBrainz, including releases absent from the listener’s library. Opening one of those albums looks for it on the listener’s connected music services, with an option to add it to the library.

Albums that are only catalogue entries remain visibly marked as outside the library and do not offer a play button. If none of the connected services carries the album, Music Assistant explains that it is unavailable there.
Marcel van der Veldt extends the cross-service linking reported on September 28 from matching music already held to discovering what an artist’s wider catalogue contains.

articles.title: Home Assistant removes music-service credentials from Sonos diagnostics
articles.dek: Troubleshooting exports omit stored authentication data whose encryption can be broken.
body: Home Assistant removes Sonos music-service authentication data from its diagnostic exports. Sharing that data could expose keys for connected music services despite the encryption around it.
Contributor jjlawren strips the affected third-party media-server entries, citing a report that their encryption has been broken. J. Nick Koston reviewed the correction.

pullRequests.title: Sanitize Sonos diagnostics

articles.title: Home Assistant finds battery charge on more SolarEdge inverters
articles.dek: A fallback reading helps Home Hub systems that do not expose a separate battery device.
body: Home Assistant adds a battery-charge percentage for some SolarEdge Home Hub inverters that expose no separate battery through their local connection. The reading appears on the inverter itself; capacity, health and power remain unavailable.

Franck Nijhof’s fallback requires an installer-set grid profile supporting IEEE 1547-2018. To avoid reporting batteries where none exist, it appears only after a nonzero charge reading at setup. A real battery at exactly zero needs an integration reload after it gains charge.

articles.title: ESPHome finds devices on IPv6-only networks
articles.dek: Device Builder stops showing reachable devices as offline when their discovery messages use IPv6.
body: ESPHome Device Builder finds devices whose discovery messages arrive over IPv6, instead of leaving them marked offline or unknown. Linux and Windows hosts can listen over both IPv4 and IPv6; macOS and FreeBSD hosts using both still listen only over IPv4.
Roman Priesol verified the correction with IPv6-only devices behind a UniFi discovery relay and in a Linux container. This is his first contribution to Device Builder, reviewed by J. Nick Koston.

pullRequests.title: Bind the mDNS responder on IPv6 as well as IPv4

articles.title: ESPHome keeps wired audio from exhausting device memory
articles.dek: Boards configured for both Wi-Fi and Ethernet move received network data into their larger external memory.
body: ESPHome moves received Ethernet data into external memory on compatible boards configured for both Wi-Fi and Ethernet. In J. Nick Koston’s Sendspin test on an Apollo CAST-1, streaming previously exhausted internal memory within a second; the correction left 22.8 KB free.
The change requires external memory and a W5500, DM9051, CH390 or ENC28J60 Ethernet chip. Wi-Fi-only and Ethernet-only configurations keep their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: [ethernet] Move received frames to PSRAM on SPI ethernet chips

articles.title: Piper preserves learned progress when voice training resumes
articles.dek: Resuming a saved run no longer silently restores the original voice model.
body: People training local Piper voices avoid a failure that could silently reset a resumed run to its starting voice model. A saved setting could reload the original weights after the checkpoint restored the trained ones, while still reporting the later training stage.

Michael Hansen also restores the intended gradual reduction in learning rate. A published English base checkpoint still had its initial rates after 549,164 training steps. Fixed-length runs derive the reduction from their chosen duration; open-ended runs retain the older defaults.

roadmapUpdates.title: Infrared remote support moves into Building
roadmapUpdates.summary: Matthias Kerstner moved infrared remote support from Shaping to Building, citing work by DAB-LABS. The opportunity aims to make brand-specific integrations easier to create using the community HAIR project; this is a development step, with no release date established.

roadmapUpdates.title: Web contributions to the device database receive approval
roadmapUpdates.summary: The proposal for limited, moderated device-data changes through the website and public Git repository moves from Awaiting approval to Approved, with Medium priority. Matthias Kerstner says a Lisbon summit session agreed its main pillars; anonymous submissions remain outside the scope.

sources.title: Enable first iteration of contributing to the device database via the web interface

roadmapUpdates.title: Home Assistant marks its design direction work complete
roadmapUpdates.summary: The brand-personality and visual-direction opportunities are marked Done. Their scope defines how Home Assistant should feel and establishes a shared visual direction; it explicitly excludes a product redesign or frontend implementation.

sources.title: Defining the Home Assistant brand personality
Define visual design direction for Home Assistant

roadmapUpdates.title: Two-way camera audio moves to approval review
roadmapUpdates.summary: The proposal for speaking through compatible cameras and doorbells moves from Shaping to Awaiting approval. It aims for a shared capability across the web interface and both companion apps, using WebRTC connections and explicit user activation; approval and release remain pending.
